facts.raw_span: A woman in her 30s with a history of right breast cancer, stage IIIa (cT2N2M0)
pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site of the right breast
The lesion did not respond to initial topical treatments
A well-demarcated, warm, erythematous plaque, 15 × 12 cm, was seen over the right side of the anterior chest wall around her operation scar
Scattered within the erythema were multiple palpable small nodules
Negative for estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)
Multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels
Right mastectomy scar with a large well-defined area of erythema and multiple, scattered small nodules
Nearly complete remission of skin lesions after treatment

concepts.why: The patient has a history of right breast cancer and presents with a pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site, which is consistent with inflammatory breast cancer recurrence.
The presence of multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels supports the diagnosis of cutaneous metastasis of breast cancer.
The patient received radiation therapy and presents with a pruritic erythema lesion with multiple nodules over the operation site, which is consistent with radiation dermatitis.

The patient presents with a well-demarcated, warm, erythematous plaque with multiple palpable small nodules, but the etiology is uncertain and could be related to cancer recurrence, radiation-induced skin changes, or other dermatological conditions.
The negative immunohistochemistry results for ER, PR, and HER2 explain the uncovered fact of the cancer cells being triple-negative.

rationales.F01: History of breast cancer increases likelihood of recurrence or metastasis
rationales.F04: Well-demarcated erythematous plaque with nodules is suggestive of inflammatory breast cancer recurrence or cutaneous metastasis
rationales.F06: Triple-negative breast cancer is more likely to be aggressive and metastasize
rationales.F07: Presence of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels is diagnostic of metastasis

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of multiple emboli of carcinoma cells in dermal and subcutaneous lymphatic vessels, as seen in the skin biopsy, strongly supports the diagnosis of cutaneous metastasis of breast cancer, which is a more specific finding than the characteristics of the erythematous plaque alone.
